### Project Name

URACE

### Project Description

### 1. Project Overview
* **Project Name:** Universal Recursive Autonomous Co-Founder Engine (URACE)
* **Repository URL:** https://github.com/joaoalbertocsjunior/URACE
* **Primary Author/Maintainer:** joaoalbertocsjunior
* **License:** CC0 1.0 Universal (Public Domain Dedication)
* **Requested Maturity Phase:** Growth / Sandbox

### 2. Executive Summary & Paradigm Shift
The primary objective of this submission is to introduce a fundamental paradigm shift in how open-source multi-agent infrastructure is built: moving away from rigid, brittle open-source code libraries and toward reusable architectural blueprint specifications.

Traditional open-source agent tools suffer from severe dependency bloat, strict runtime constraints, and vendor lock-in. URACE breaks this mold by delivering a completely portable, install-as-bootstrap standard (`URACE.md`) composed of 72 independent, reusable building blocks (patterns, schemas, mechanisms, and contracts). 

Instead of forcing developers to download heavy software packages, URACE allows them to selectively derive, import, and adapt structural primitives—such as cognitive resumes, authority boundaries, and regression gates—natively into any codebase. It shifts the open-source focus from distributing pre-packaged programs to distributing foundational, universally applicable structural designs.

### 3. Core Ecosystem Alignment
URACE is designed to serve as a complementary orchestration and context-governance specification layer that sits directly on top of existing foundational AAIF technologies:

* **The Dynamic Counterpart to AGENTS.md:** While AGENTS.md establishes static, repository-level guidelines for incoming developer agents, URACE functions as the active runtime loop—interpreting goals, enforcing protected boundaries, and tracking evolutionary states.
* **Orchestration Layer for MCP & Goose:** URACE completely decouples lifecycle logic from execution mechanics. It cleanly intakes Model Context Protocol (MCP) compliant clients or servers (such as Goose) as pluggable, replaceable "Executors" to run code modifications, while URACE itself handles systemic validation and rule checking.

### 4. Technical Contributions to the Specification Era
By focusing on a blueprint-first pattern library, URACE brings several unique primitives to the open-source agentic architectural landscape:
* **Token-Preserving Lifecycle Compaction:** A standardized protocol for gradually compressing linear execution logs (`urace /compact`) into a semantic Cognitive Resume to prevent context window decay over long recursive runs.
* **Deterministic Rule-Graph Tracking:** Every product change is permanently mapped to a queryable snapshot graph of active rules (`urace /rules`), introducing a pattern for tracing agent actions back to explicit human-defined permissions.
* **Zero-Dependency Portability:** The entire runtime loop specification operates through a single bootstrap document, triggering structural commands natively via an environment-appropriate launcher.

### 5. Current Project Status
The specification and its 72 core building blocks are fully outlined and dedicated to the public domain (CC0 1.0). Bringing this project under the umbrella of the AAIF will allow the Technical Committee and working groups to help standardize this blueprint-driven paradigm, transforming how developers engineer resilient multi-agent orchestration loops globally.


### Preferred Lifecycle Stage (if known)

Sandbox

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

URACE fosters open, secure, and runtime-agnostic agent orchestration. By moving the industry away from heavy, fragmented codebases and toward reusable blueprint standards, it ensures multi-agent lifecycles can be safely governed without vendor lock-in.

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

• Direct horizontal synergy. It acts as the dynamic, state-tracking runtime loop to complement the static repository guidelines of AGENTS.md. It treats engines like Anthropic's MCP (Model Context Protocol) or Goose as modular, pluggable "Executors," orchestrating them without interfering with their internal codebases.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

• Use Case 1: Continuous software repository evolution under strict boundary rules using the urace /auto protocol.
• Use Case 2: Selective injection of individual patterns (e.g., executing urace derive "authority boundary model") to inject security contracts into custom enterprise Python or TypeScript agent frameworks.
• Evidence: Core specification is live and functional via the open blueprint file layout at https://github.com/joaoalbertocsjunior/URACE

### Governance Model

The project operates under an open-source maintainer framework, moving toward an official AAIF Working Group structure upon sandbox acceptance.

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

Maintained natively via the GitHub repository. Because this project is an open specification standard rather than packaged software binaries, releases are versioned based on changes to the core contract models and schemas.

### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

Anyone can suggest modifications, edits, or add new building blocks to the specification by opening an Issue or submitting a Pull Request against the core URACE.md file.

### Publicly Accessible Issue Tracker

https://github.com/joaoalbertocsjunior/URACE/issues

### External Project Dependencies

The specification is written entirely in Markdown, ensuring absolute portable agnosticism across runtimes.
